bottleneck: The blood-brain barrier excludes 98% of small molecules and nearly all biologics from the brain, making CNS drug development uniquely punishing: most neurological drugs are discovered by luck or repurposing rather than design, because rationally designed molecules cannot reach their targets. Delivery workarounds each carry heavy costs — focused ultrasound opening risks admitting pathogens, shuttle peptides work only for specific cargo, intrathecal pumps are invasive and distribute poorly through parenchyma. The barrier that protects the brain from toxins defeats almost every systemic therapy for it, forcing developers to choose between no delivery and unsafe delivery.
current_state: Antibody shuttles exploiting transferrin receptors and receptor-mediated transport show early promise in trials, but no general platform delivers arbitrary drugs across the human BBB.

sources.title: Architecting the Future of Health: From Code to Cure

title: Blood-brain barrier excludes most CNS drugs
why_it_blocks: The barrier is the single biggest reason CNS drug pipelines fail. Nearly every neurological disease is harder to treat because drugs cannot get in — cracking it would unlock the entire shelved pharmacopeia of brain therapeutics.
